key_insight: Regularization makes ill-posed inverse problems tractable, while data-driven methods aim to improve reconstruction quality without sacrificing reliability.
engineering_relevance: Reliable reconstruction from indirect measurements is critical in applications such as medical imaging, where algorithmic artifacts can be mistaken for physical abnormalities.
method: Establish classical regularization theory for inverse problems.
Develop variational formulations and optimization algorithms for reconstruction.
Examine unrolling, learned regularizers, and plug-and-play methods alongside their performance guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a course-style treatment of theory and algorithms but reports no datasets, quantitative benchmarks, or experimental results.
watch_item: Data-driven improvements may come at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees, requiring careful validation in safety-critical applications.
